why: Vi follows Jarvan IV wherever he goes: Cease and Desist stays locked on through his flag-and-drag escape, so his own engage becomes his isolation. Inside Cataclysm she out-duels him with Denting Blows percent-health damage and armor shred, and Vault Breaker gives her a second dash to chase or leave once the cage drops. She won 58% of 31 pro games in this pairing.
tips: Hold Cease and Desist until Jarvan IV has used his flag combo, then lock onto him so he cannot drag himself away.
Charge Vault Breaker to leave Cataclysm only after Jarvan IV has spent his knock-up, so the dash cannot be interrupted.
Attack Jarvan IV in short repeated bursts to keep Denting Blows shredding his armor before a full commit.

why: Pantheon answers Lee Sin's early skirmishing with a point-and-click stun that Lee Sin cannot dodge, then blocks the return burst by facing him with Aegis Assault. Empowered Comet Spears win the level-3 duel before Lee Sin's mobility comes online, and Grand Starfall lets Pantheon answer Lee Sin's ganks across the map instead of chasing him through the jungle. Pantheon took 57% of 21 pro games here.
tips: Open duels with Shield Vault only when your passive is stacked, so the empowered Comet Spear follows the stun.
Face Lee Sin with Aegis Assault as soon as he lands Sonic Wave, so his second cast and autos hit the shield.
Use Grand Starfall toward the lane Lee Sin is ganking rather than spending it to chase him through warded jungle.

why: Naafiri's Packmates stand between her and Vi, so Vault Breaker keeps colliding with a hound instead of the champion Vi wants to lock down. When Vi does commit, Naafiri's burst, bleed and healing from her daggers out-trade Vi's shield in the extended fight, and her ultimate's brief untargetability plus extra Packmates make the follow-up messy. The pairing is close in pro play, at 55% for Naafiri over 20 games.
tips: Throw Darkin Daggers from behind your Packmates so Vi must walk through them to reach you.
Save your ultimate for the moment Vi starts her ultimate dash, then use the extra Packmates to swarm her on landing.
Dash away after landing both daggers and re-engage once the bleed and healing have won the first trade.

why: Pantheon punishes Vi's telegraphed engage: Shield Vault stuns her out of a Vault Breaker charge, and Aegis Assault turned toward her soaks the burst that follows Cease and Desist. His empowered early damage wins duels before Vi finishes her first item, which is why pro teams went 63% with him over 19 games. Grand Starfall also matches Vi's gank pressure without needing to walk through her jungle.
tips: Stun Vi while she is charging Vault Breaker to cancel the dash and leave her stranded in front of your team.
Turn Aegis Assault toward Vi the instant her ultimate lands on you, then counter with an empowered Comet Spear.
Gank with Grand Starfall before Vi reaches level 6, while her only engage is a charge she must telegraph.

why: Lee Sin never has to stand where Skarner wants him: Safeguard and Resonating Strike let him leave Ixtal's Impact charges and re-enter on his own timing. Dragon's Rage is the cleanest answer to Impale in the game, kicking Skarner away from the teammate he is dragging or out of a fight before he can cast it. Lee Sin's stronger early dueling also lets him contest Skarner's first clears instead of conceding the river.
tips: Kick Skarner away the moment he grabs a teammate with Impale, so the drag ends far from his team.
Ward-hop out of Ixtal's Impact instead of flashing, and re-engage with Sonic Wave once the charge is spent.
Invade Skarner's second buff with a lane that can move first, while he is still too slow to win a straight duel.

why: Lee Sin plays through Paranoia better than most junglers because Sonic Wave and Tempest reveal Nocturne once they connect, so the darkness does not hide him after his dive lands. Safeguard moves Lee Sin straight to the teammate Nocturne is diving, and Dragon's Rage kicks Nocturne off before the fear tether completes. Before level 6 Lee Sin also wins the river duels that decide who reaches their ultimate first.
tips: Safeguard to the teammate Nocturne dives and kick him away before his fear tether finishes channeling.
Land Sonic Wave on Nocturne during Paranoia to keep him revealed for your team while vision is down.
Fight Nocturne for the early scuttles and his second buff to delay his level 6 as long as possible.

why: Nocturne turns Jarvan IV's engage against him: Shroud of Darkness blocks the flag-combo knock-up or the Cataclysm follow-up, and once Jarvan IV has dashed in he has no way out of the fear tether. Paranoia also answers Jarvan IV anywhere on the map, diving the back line while Jarvan IV is stuck at the front. Pro teams won 67% of 15 games with this answer.
tips: Pop Shroud of Darkness as Jarvan IV's flag lands, so his dash knocks up nothing and strands him in your team.
Cast Paranoia in response to a Cataclysm engage and dive the carries he left behind.
Stay on Jarvan IV after he dashes in so the fear tether completes while he has no escape left.

why: Cataclysm is close to a hard counter to Naafiri's kit: her dashes need a target or a short hop, and neither crosses the cage wall, so she and her Packmates are trapped in a small circle with Jarvan IV. His flag combo knocks her up mid-dash, his passive hits for percent health through her healing, and she has no way to reach the back line she wants. Jarvan IV won 92% of 12 pro games in this pairing.
tips: Save Cataclysm until Naafiri has used her dash, then cage her so she cannot reach your carries.
Aim the flag combo at the spot Naafiri's dash will land, not at where she starts it.
Drop your flag inside the cage for the attack speed buff and keep auto-attacking to refresh your percent-health passive hit.

why: Xin Zhao beats Vi at her own game of committing fully: Crescent Guard knocks her team away and makes him immune to damage from outside the circle, so a Cease and Desist dive becomes a one-on-one he is built to win. His passive healing and Three Talon Strike sustain through her burst, and Audacious Charge sticks to her when she tries to Vault Breaker away. He won 75% of 12 pro games here.
tips: Cast Crescent Guard right after Vi's ultimate lands on you to knock her team away and duel her alone.
Hold Audacious Charge until Vi starts Vault Breaker, then dash to her so she cannot create distance.
Keep auto-attacking through her burst instead of retreating, since your passive healing rewards staying in the fight.

why: Nocturne removes Pantheon's most reliable tool by spell-shielding Shield Vault, the point-and-click stun his whole early game is built around. Once the stun is gone, the fear tether wins the extended duel because Pantheon's damage is front-loaded into one rotation. Paranoia then matches Grand Starfall's global pressure and usually arrives with more damage behind it.
tips: Hold Shroud of Darkness for Shield Vault and cast it as Pantheon leaps, so his stun fizzles.
Stay in auto-attack range after shielding the stun so the fear tether completes before he can disengage.
Use Paranoia to answer Grand Starfall landings and dive the same target Pantheon jumped to.

why: Skarner simply does not die to Pantheon's first rotation: his health stacking and shield absorb the empowered Comet Spear burst that kills squishier junglers. While Pantheon waits on cooldowns, Ixtal's Impact can run him into a wall, and Impale suppresses him so he cannot raise Aegis Assault or stun his way out while Skarner's team collapses. That durability flipped the early-game matchup to 60% for Skarner over 10 pro games.
tips: Drag Pantheon toward your team with Impale before he can raise his shield, so he takes the full collapse.
Take the first Comet Spear trade without retreating, then charge him once his empowered passive is spent.
Charge Ixtal's Impact along walls near Pantheon so the carry distance ends in a stun, not open ground.

why: Nocturne punishes Naafiri for doing the one thing she must do, which is stay glued to her target: the fear tether completes while she and her Packmates are committed, and Shroud of Darkness can eat a Darkin Dagger or her dash follow-up. His Duskbringer trail also lets him match her movement during her ultimate and keep auto-attacking after her burst ends. Pro teams won 67% of 9 games answering Naafiri this way.
tips: Tether Naafiri the moment she dashes onto you and keep walking with her so the fear triggers.
Save Shroud of Darkness for her second dagger cast to deny the healing her trade depends on.
Answer her ultimate with Paranoia onto her target's lane partner to turn her all-in into a numbers fight.

why: Qiyana fights where Naafiri is weakest, in the river and against jungle walls: Supreme Display of Talent knocks Naafiri into terrain for the stun and burst window, and brush-element Edge of Ixtal makes Qiyana invisible so Packmates lose their target mid-trade. Her faster burst also lands before Naafiri's bleed and healing can turn the duel. It is a thin pro sample, so treat the edge as kit-based rather than proven.
tips: Pick up the brush element before trading with Naafiri so her Packmates drop target on you mid-fight.
Start fights near a wall or in the river, where your ultimate and river root both reach full value.
Burst Naafiri and dash out before her daggers come back up, rather than staying for a second rotation.

why: Trundle stat-checks Nocturne's dive: Chomp steals the attack damage Nocturne's whole kit scales on, and Subjugate drains health and resistances through the fear window instead of dying to it. Pillar of Ice also cuts off Nocturne's approach or escape in the jungle corridors where Paranoia dives happen. Once the first rotation fails, Trundle's sustained autos and healing win every extra second of the fight.
tips: Cast Subjugate on Nocturne as soon as he lands on you, so his dive window is spent fighting drained stats.
Place Pillar of Ice behind Nocturne when he dives, so he cannot walk out after the fear ends.
Keep auto-attacking on your Frozen Domain instead of chasing, and let Chomp's stolen damage stack up.

why: Trundle attacks Naafiri's damage itself: Chomp steals a chunk of the attack damage her daggers and Packmates scale from, and Subjugate drains her resistances while healing him through her bleed. Pillar of Ice slows her and the pack in jungle chokepoints, and his sustained damage does not care about her short untargetable moment the way a burst combo would. The pro sample is small and the games are older, so keep expectations modest.
tips: Open every duel with Chomp to cut Naafiri's damage before her Packmates start stacking hits.
Drop Pillar of Ice between Naafiri and her escape path once she dashes in, then fight on Frozen Domain.
Save Subjugate for her ultimate window, when the extra Packmates make a fast kill matter most.

why: Nocturne is one of the few junglers who can say no to Cease and Desist: a well-timed Shroud of Darkness blocks Vi's engage tool, leaving her without lockdown while the fear tether channels. If Vi instead charges Vault Breaker in, Nocturne out-duels her with Duskbringer's attack damage and passive healing. Paranoia then punishes Vi's next commit by counter-diving in darkness while her ultimate is down.
tips: Time Shroud of Darkness for Vi's ultimate cast so her lockdown is spent and her team cannot follow.
Tether Vi immediately after shielding her engage and stay in range until the fear lands.
Dive with Paranoia during the window after Vi has used her ultimate on someone else.

why: Wukong's clone eats the one ability Pantheon cannot afford to waste: Warrior Trickster leaves a decoy that can take Shield Vault's stun while the real Wukong repositions. His passive stacks armor and regeneration the longer Pantheon stays in, which blunts the burst-then-stun pattern, and Cyclone's knock-up interrupts Pantheon's shield stance and second engage. Wukong won 86% of a small 7-game pro sample.
tips: Tap Warrior Trickster as Pantheon leaps with Shield Vault so the clone takes the stun.
Cast Cyclone when Pantheon raises his shield stance, then use the second spin after he tries to re-engage.
Extend trades past Pantheon's first rotation, where your stacking armor and regeneration take over.

why: Wukong breaks Lee Sin's combo at its first step, since Sonic Wave can land on the clone left by Warrior Trickster while the real Wukong steps out of the follow-up dash. Crashing Blow shreds Lee Sin's armor for the extended trade his passive is built to win, and Cyclone knocks Lee Sin up through his second engage instead of letting him kick and leave. Pro teams took 71% of 7 games with this answer.
tips: Leave your clone in Lee Sin's Sonic Wave path and step sideways before he takes the second cast.
Shred Lee Sin with Crashing Blow before casting Cyclone, so both spins hit reduced armor.
Save your second Cyclone spin for Lee Sin's attempt to safeguard out, and dash after him with Nimbus Strike.

why: Naafiri's Packmates keep attacking through Wukong's tricks better than a single-target duelist does, surrounding him after Warrior Trickster so the brief invisibility buys less distance, and her daggers give her healing in the long trade after Cyclone ends. Her dash also lets her re-stick to the real Wukong once the clone fades. The pro edge is real but small at 7 games, and the exact clone interaction is hard to verify without watching the games, so treat this one cautiously.
tips: Send Packmates in first and hold your dash until Wukong's clone has faded, then jump the real champion.
Land both Darkin Daggers before committing, so the bleed and healing carry the trade after Cyclone.
Use your ultimate after Wukong spins, when his knock-up is gone and the extra Packmates can finish him.

why: Jarvan IV answers Skarner's charge with a faster interrupt: the flag combo's knock-up stops Ixtal's Impact before it reaches a wall or a carry. Cataclysm then splits Skarner from the team following his engage, and Jarvan IV's percent-health passive plus flag attack speed let him actually damage the health stacker inside the cage. He took 71% of 7 pro games in the pairing.
tips: Aim your flag combo across Skarner's charge path to knock him up before he reaches your back line.
Cage Skarner after his charge ends, away from the teammates who would follow his ultimate.
Keep your flag down during objective fights so your team gets attack speed while you hold Skarner off.

why: Trundle removes Lee Sin's early-game edge by stealing his attack damage with Chomp, turning the level-3 duel Lee Sin usually dictates into a stat check he loses. Pillar of Ice in a jungle corridor blocks the second Sonic Wave dash or the safeguard escape, and Trundle does not fall off the way Lee Sin does once teamfights start. Subjugate later drains whatever durability Lee Sin builds to survive.
tips: Bite Lee Sin at the start of every duel so his combo damage drops before he can finish it.
Place Pillar of Ice on Lee Sin's ward-hop escape route when he tries to leave a losing trade.
Fight inside Frozen Domain near river entrances, where Lee Sin has fewer walls to escape over.

why: Pantheon wins the first exchange against Jarvan IV by stunning him as he commits and blocking the return damage with Aegis Assault, and his empowered spear damage is higher before either jungler has items. Jarvan IV's cage also helps Pantheon in one way: it holds Jarvan IV still in spear range with no room to dodge. Grand Starfall then lets Pantheon beat Jarvan IV to plays instead of walking into flag combos.
tips: Stun Jarvan IV the moment his flag lands, before his dash can knock you up.
Face your shield stance into the Cataclysm wall fight so his autos and spear hit Aegis Assault.
Jump lanes with Grand Starfall while Jarvan IV shows on a ward, arriving before he can walk there.

why: Vi is built to kill exactly what Trundle becomes: Denting Blows deals percent-health damage and shreds armor on every third hit, so Subjugate's stolen resistances and health stack melt faster than Trundle expects. Cease and Desist pins him in place so he cannot kite her on Frozen Domain, and Vault Breaker lets her leave while Subjugate ticks and re-engage after it expires. She won 57% of 7 pro games here.
tips: Count your Denting Blows procs on Trundle and keep attacking until the armor shred stacks before using abilities.
Vault Breaker away when Trundle casts Subjugate, then re-engage once the drain has expired.
Lock Trundle down with your ultimate at the start of objective fights so he cannot pillar your team off the pit.

why: Lee Sin out-maneuvers Xin Zhao's one-way engage: Audacious Charge needs its mark and a straight line, while Lee Sin has two dashes and a ward hop to choose when the duel actually happens. Dragon's Rage kicks Xin Zhao away from the team he charged into, wasting Crescent Guard's protected circle far from anyone he wants to hit. Lee Sin's early burst also contests Xin Zhao's first clear instead of conceding it.
tips: Kick Xin Zhao away as soon as he dashes in, so his ultimate circle protects him from nobody.
Ward-hop out after his knock-up combo starts and re-engage with Sonic Wave while his dash is down.
Meet Xin Zhao at his second buff with a laner who can arrive first, before his sustain items come online.

why: Pantheon beats Trundle before Trundle becomes a stat wall: Shield Vault stops Chomp trades on Pantheon's terms, Aegis Assault blocks the autos Trundle needs to sustain, and empowered Comet Spears chunk him before Frozen Domain healing matters. Grand Starfall also lets Pantheon snowball lanes while Trundle is still farming toward his spike. The games behind this are older, so the read is early-pressure based.
tips: Stun Trundle as he steps onto Frozen Domain and finish the trade before his healing stacks up.
Turn Aegis Assault toward Trundle during his all-in so his autos hit the shield instead of healing him.
Gank early and often with Grand Starfall rather than farming beside Trundle into the late game.

why: Xin Zhao survives the burst Pantheon relies on and wins what comes after: Crescent Guard shrugs off damage from Pantheon's team while he duels, his passive healing outlasts one spear rotation, and Audacious Charge sticks through Pantheon's attempt to walk away. Three Talon Strike's knock-up also interrupts Aegis Assault positioning. The sample is older, so this is a durability read more than a current-meta lock.
tips: Dash onto Pantheon after he spends his empowered spear, so his strongest hit is already gone.
Cast Crescent Guard when Pantheon's team collapses on you and keep dueling him inside the circle.
Knock Pantheon up as he raises his shield stance to break his positioning and keep auto-attacking.

why: Qiyana denies Pantheon his guaranteed stun: with a brush element held, Edge of Ixtal turns her invisible, and a point-and-click Shield Vault cannot be cast on a target Pantheon cannot see. In the jungle she also fights next to walls, where Supreme Display of Talent stuns Pantheon for her full burst before his shield stance matters. Pro teams won all 6 games sampled, though that is too few to call proven.
tips: Hold a brush element whenever Pantheon is near, and go invisible the moment he walks at you.
Drag fights toward jungle walls so your ultimate stuns Pantheon before he can raise his shield.
Dash out after your burst and wait for the next element instead of trading autos with Pantheon.

why: Xin Zhao isolates the real fight inside Wukong's tricks: Crescent Guard knocks the clone and Wukong's team away, and his sustain wins the standing duel after Cyclone's first knock-up. Audacious Charge follows Wukong's Nimbus Strike engage, and his healing passive rewards exactly the extended auto-attack trade Wukong's passive wants to shorten with burst. He won 83% of 6 pro games here.
tips: Wait for Wukong's clone to appear before dashing, so Audacious Charge lands on the real champion.
Cast Crescent Guard as Cyclone starts to knock Wukong's team out of the fight around him.
Stay in the duel after the first spin ends, since your healing wins the trade from that point.

why: Cho'Gath answers Naafiri with control she cannot dash through: Feral Scream silences her mid-combo so the second dagger and dash follow-up come late, Rupture threatens the spot her dash lands, and his Feast-stacked health pool is too large for her bleed burst to finish. Feast plus Smite also takes neutral objectives off the table in any contest she tries to force. Jungle Cho'Gath is rare in pro play and the sample is only 6 games, so this is the least certain entry in the set.
tips: Silence Naafiri as soon as she dashes in, so her combo stalls before the second dagger.
Place Rupture where her dash will land rather than where she starts it.
Stack Feast on large jungle monsters early so your health pool outgrows her burst before first dragon fights.

why: Jarvan IV keeps Wukong where his team can hit him: Cataclysm's walls block the short Warrior Trickster dash, so the clone appears inside the cage with the real Wukong still in range of follow-up damage. The flag combo can knock Wukong up out of Nimbus Strike before Cyclone starts, and Jarvan IV's percent-health passive works through the armor Wukong's passive stacks. He won 67% of 6 pro games here.
tips: Save Cataclysm until Wukong has used his clone dash, then cage him with no way across the wall.
Knock Wukong up with your flag combo as he dashes in, before his first Cyclone spin starts.
Keep hitting Wukong between his spins so your percent-health passive keeps working through his armor.

why: Wukong gives Paranoia a bad target: Warrior Trickster can leave a clone in the dive path and let the real Wukong step out of the fear tether's range before it completes. If Nocturne lands anyway, Cyclone knocks him up through the tether channel and Wukong's stacking armor blunts the Duskbringer trade. The mechanism is plausible and the pro sample is 6 games at 67%, but the clone-versus-dive timing is hard to confirm without watching those games.
tips: Leave your clone toward Nocturne as Paranoia starts and step away before his dash arrives.
Cast Cyclone the moment Nocturne lands on you to knock him up before his fear completes.
Dash to Nocturne with Nimbus Strike after his spell shield is spent, then shred his armor with Crashing Blow.

why: Trundle steals the stats Wukong's passive works so hard to stack: Subjugate drains a percentage of his health, armor and magic resistance mid-Cyclone, and Chomp cuts the attack damage behind Crashing Blow. Pillar of Ice also pins Wukong after his clone dash, in the corridor fights Trundle chooses. Once Cyclone is spent, Trundle's sustained damage and healing win the rest of the fight.
tips: Cast Subjugate on Wukong as his first Cyclone spin starts, so he fights the whole engage drained.
Save Pillar of Ice until Wukong's clone has faded, then block the real champion's exit.
Bite Wukong before he casts Crashing Blow on you so his armor-shredded autos hit for less.

why: Vi brings the two things Skarner's health stacking hates: Denting Blows percent-health damage with armor shred, and an ultimate that cannot be stopped on the way in, so Impale cannot peel her off his team's carry during her dash. She can also Vault Breaker out of Ixtal's Impact lines instead of being run into a wall. In the pit, her burst plus Smite contests objectives before Skarner's slower damage matters.
tips: Save your ultimate for Skarner's carry target and dash through him rather than dueling him first.
Vault Breaker sideways out of Ixtal's Impact charges instead of running in a straight line.
Keep Denting Blows stacked on Skarner during objective dances so his health pool shrinks before the smite fight.
